# Data Governance as Code

By Rolling Edition, with AI · **In practice** · [Read it free online](https://rollingedition.com/data-governance-as-code)

[![The latest edition's stamp](https://rollingedition.com/data-governance-as-code/stamp.svg)](https://rollingedition.com/data-governance-as-code) [![Checks](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-data-governance-as-code/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-data-governance-as-code/actions/workflows/checks.yml)

Governing a data platform with code that runs in CI: a catalog where every table has an owner and every column a classification, personal data found automatically, lineage from pipelines, access policies as tested Rego enforced as row filters and column masks, retention, consent and erasure that remove data, an audit trail, and the same rules for data that trains or grounds AI.

**Written with AI. Verified by people.** [How we make books](https://rollingedition.com/policies/editorial) · [Check a copy](https://rollingedition.com/check)

## Who it's for

For data, analytics and platform engineers who already build pipelines and warehouses and have been asked to make them governed: comfortable with SQL, Python and Parquet, and looking for governance that is tested and reviewed like the rest of their code.

## Run the examples

Every example runs offline, in a pinned environment, and its output must match the book's. With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```sh
uv venv --python 3.12.15
uv pip install -r examples/requirements.txt
cd examples && ../.venv/bin/python catalog-the-learners.py
```

Model outputs are recorded once in `examples/data/recorded/`, each folder with a `manifest.json` that names the model, its exact version and the script that recorded it, so the examples never call a model. `recordings/` holds the scripts that record them again.

Where the data comes from, and its licence: [`examples/data/platform/README.md`](examples/data/platform/README.md).

## How this book stays current

When a library this book uses releases a new version, every example runs again in the new version. Agents draft any fix and check every change, and a change merges once its checks pass; one with a serious risk, such as a security or copyright problem, waits for a Rolling Edition maintainer. Anyone can check the book or correct it with a pull request. Each new edition is stamped with its date, its examples passing and what changed. [See what changed in each edition](https://rollingedition.com/data-governance-as-code/changes).
